author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Although booster exploded, company caught upper stage for first time in campaign to make megarocket reusable

SpaceX’s megarocket Starship returned to its Texas launch tower on Saturday, a milestone in the company’s efforts to make the craft suitable for human spaceflight.

The 171ft (52-meter) bullet-shaped upper stage descended into the clutch of the tower’s mechanical arms, ending a 22hr mission where the craft orbited Earth 14 times.

Continue reading...
title: SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit in victory for company

author: Jack Seale
description:
This tale of a young female spy in 1980s East Berlin is a visual delight. Around every corner is a fun comic twist

Is there any more alluring aesthetic in screen fiction than the iron curtain thriller? Any TV show dealing in 1980s cold war chic – Deutschland 83, Kleo, Star City, The Same Sky, the Russian bits of The Americans – probably has an irresistible mix of danger, absurdity and exotic kitsch. Moustaches! Wigs! Leather trench coats! Rigid patterned fabrics! Cassette players! Boxy cars! The chilly ennui of oppressed citizens and the flagrant risk-taking of secret agents, all somehow liberated by an existential inner emptiness! It’s just so much fun.

Honey pitches us straight into premium frosty paranoia with an opening scene in which British “press attache” – ie spy handler – Graham Anderson (Rory Kinnear, hoorah!) endures a nervous crossing back into East Berlin, during which he really, really does not want his car to be searched. The crowning indignity of his int
title: Honey review – a hugely entertaining Killing Eve prequel that’s packed with naughty jokes

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Canadian lineman died Friday after medical incident

  • Three-star prospect committed to Georgia in June

  • High school postpones game as coach pays tribute

Marcellus Young Casario, an 18-year-old Canadian high school football player who had committed to Georgia, died Friday following what his school described as a medical emergency.

Casario, a senior defensive lineman at Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School in northeast Georgia, was taken to hospital after an incident Friday morning. The school announced his death later that day but did not identify him until Saturday. No further details about the circumstances were released.

Continue reading...
title: Georgia football recruit Marcellus Young Casario dies at 18 after medical emergency

author: Agencies
description:
• Home side avenge October defeat in Cardiff

  • Wales bottom of Group A4 with one game left

Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Norway in Oslo to dent their hopes of staying in the top tier of the Nations League.

Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup struck in the space of nine second-half minutes as Norway turned the screw.

Continue reading...
title: Clinical Norway dent Wales’ Nations League top-tier hopes with victory in Oslo

author: Joti Birdi
description:
• Original No 7 design preserved to honour player

  • Career brought 146 goals and three major titles

Portugal have made a permanent change to the No 7 shirt to honour the legacy of Cristiano Ronaldo and ensure the number remains forever associated with their greatest footballing icon.

The former forward, whose career spanned 23 years and 246 caps in which he scored 146 goals, announced his retirement on 5 November after a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus. His last appearance for Portugal was on 24 September, in a 1-0 home win over Wales in the Nations League.

Continue reading...
title: Portugal immortalise Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt in tribute to national legend

author: Christopher Hopkins and Stephanie Convery
description:
They number more than half a million, yet the ongoing trauma from their time in orphanages and institutions remains poorly known

When Judy Leonard entered the orphanage, she was given a bed with a number. That was how the staff would refer to her. Not by her name, or even by one of the cruel nicknames the other children gave her, but by her allocated space in the dormitory: C2.

“I would like the readers to close their eyes,” Judy says now, “and imagine that it was them at age nine.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’m still trying to find out who I am’: the little-understood plight of Forgotten Australians

author: Anthony Ashdown
description:
On Anthony Ashdown’s first date with Jake, their mutual love of nerd culture felt revolutionary. Then Jake referenced a catchphrase from The Golden Girls.

  • Find more stories from the moment I knew series

Picture it. Sydney. 2015. I had weathered a nasty breakup the previous year. I had often compromised a lot of who I was and what I enjoyed to keep the other person happy. Post-breakup, I decided I would never change who I was for anyone else ever again.

I got on the apps and matched with Jake, a handsome young man 10 years younger than me. We chatted on Grindr and planned to meet for coffee and then spend the afternoon at Cronulla beach.

Continue reading...
title: The moment I knew: He quoted my favourite TV show. I blurted out, ‘Marry me!’

author: Michael Aylwin at Principality Stadium
description:
• ‘It’s nothing this group doesn’t deserve for their work’

  • Beauden Barrett: ‘Their defence felt like a brick wall’

Dewi Lake, the first Wales captain to lead his team to victory over New Zealand in 73 years, paid tribute to his teammates, who chiselled this win out of a recent history of adversity, sometimes even humiliation. At last, they gave this rugby nation reason to be proud again, as he called the win an “amazing feeling”.

“It’s nice to sit in this room and not be disappointed,” he said. “I think we got asked a lot of questions last week in terms of performance, in terms of things that went wrong. We had tough conversations in the week [after a narrow win over Japan]. We’re a group that trusts each other a lot, and to put on the field what we did today, to make history, it’s tough to put it into words really. But it is not
title: Wales’ Dewi Lake calls historic win against New Zealand ‘amazing feeling’

author: Raphael Boyd
description:
Appeal for information comes after Brenda Raymond, 80, was set on fire outside her flat on Monday

The family of an elderly woman who was set on fire outside a block of flats in Watford have said that they are “desperate for answers”.

Brenda Raymond, 80, was found set alight outside her flat on Caractacus Cottage View on Monday. She was taken to a nearby hospital, where she is in critical condition.

Continue reading...
title: Family of Watford woman set alight ‘desperate for answers’ after attack

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Port also succeeds in seizing tanker, Atlantic Asphalt, to recoup damages after it crashes into cruise ship

New Orleans port officials have filed a lawsuit seeking more than $1m in damages from the owner and operator of an asphalt tanker that crashed into a docked cruise ship on the Mississippi River in the city on Friday.

In some of the first legal consequences of Friday’s crash, the port has also obtained a federal court order authorizing the seizure of the Atlantic Asphalt tanker. The Atlantic Asphalt slammed into the American Heritage cruise ship, causing the river boat to flip onto its side, injuring more than 30 people and setting off a frantic but successful effort to pull people out of the water.

Continue reading...
title: New Orleans officials file $1m lawsuit after ‘Mississippi miracle’ tanker crash

author: Suzanne Wrack at Stamford Bridge
description:
Pragmatic, resolute and gutsy. Sonia Bompastor showed her ruthless side and delivered a tactical masterclass as Chelsea earned a 1-0 win over Manchester City and leapfrogged them at the top of the Women’s Super League.

Sandy Baltimore’s stunning strike in added time at the end of the first half was the difference, as the west London side nullified the threat of a team that had scored in each of their preceding 21 games in all competitions, delivering their first loss of the campaign.

Full report to follow

Continue reading...
title: Chelsea go top of WSL as Sandy Baltimore bullet sees off Manchester City

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
Incoming lawmakers have more in common with each other than they have divisions, even across ideological factions

Democrats who won in the midterms, including those in places previously considered off the blue map and those in Democratic strongholds, crafted their campaigns around economic populism and accountability.

Lawmakers in the anti-establishment incoming congressional class have more in common with each other than divisions, even across ideological factions. Voters sent a resounding message to work on affordability and rein in the Trump administration, and Democrats across the party have many more shared goals than Republicans, who face a more existential level of discord.

Continue reading...
title: Progressive versus moderate? Democrats deny party rift as they head into new Congress

author: Timothy Pratt
description:
James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a Cox Enterprises heir, faced a two-hour hearing about alleged support for Hamas

A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of wealthy leftwing activist and philanthropist James “Fergie” Chambers turned out to be a study in contrasts.

Chambers’s defense took most of the session to query the US citizen and detail irregularities in the Trump administration’s extradition request – several of which the Guardian has reported on – as well as the figures of Spanish law that would lead the three-judge panel to deny the request; while the prosecutor sped through his case, head down, asking Chambers no questions at all.

Continue reading...
title: How a US extradition bid over Hamas allegations put a wealthy activist before a Spanish court

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Peoria officials said a bomb was found at BioUrja Renewables and later defused; FBI said it is investigating

Residents were ordered to evacuate parts of an Illinois community on Friday after the mayor there said authorities found a bomb at a local ethanol- and alcohol-production plant.

The discovery reported at BioUrja Renewables in Peoria triggered a mandatory evacuation over a one-mile evacuation zone encompassing sections of that city as well as the adjacent municipality of East Peoria.

Continue reading...
title: Bomb found at Illinois ethanol plant, prompting evacuations

author: Sian Cain
description:
The singer on his love for Ibiza, the weirdest thing he’s done in the name of romance, and being signed up for Celebrity Traitors against his will

You were a punching bag for such a long time after You’re Beautiful became a massive hit, but your consistent good humour is deeply admirable. Does it ever get tiring?

It was a surprise, at the beginning. I was just a little guy with a dream. And when you achieve your dream, you think people would be happy for you. For them not to be happy for you, but angry with you, for your song, seems irrational, an overreaction. It is interesting how people generally want to tear people down for achieving their little dreams. But I’d had a real proper job before that [as a captain in the British army]. My friends might have been on operations in Afghanistan or Iraq, so if I were to complain to them at the time saying, “Oh, the Guardian said something really horrid about me and gave me three stars for my album” – they wou
title: James Blunt: ‘Do I have a nickname? Yes, it rhymes with blunt’

author: Elle Hunt
description:
The world has become accustomed to concerns about the male loneliness epidemic. But research suggests women are just as lonely

  • Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads

No one would think of Sasha* as lonely, least of all Sasha herself. The 38-year-old from Sydney has close and longstanding friendships, proactively keeps in touch and makes plans, and is engaged with her local community.

“All those things that you read about, about why men might be lonely – they don’t maintain one-on-one friendships, or they’re not good at reaching out, or their conversations aren’t deep and meaningful – none of those issues apply to me,” she says. “I’m a very socially connected person.”
title: ‘You have to cope’: why don’t we hear of the ‘epidemic’ of women’s loneliness?

author: Agencies
description:
• Loss in Singapore marred by unruly end to friendly

  • Argentina beaten 2-1 by Uruguay in Buenos Aires

Raphinha was sent off as Brazil crashed to a 3-2 defeat to Japan in their international friendly in Singapore. The Barcelona captain had been substituted after 71 minutes, but was shown a red card after protesting against Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s stoppage-time winner on the touchline. The Brazil head coach, Carlo Ancelotti, was also sent off in a fractious ending to the match.

Japan went 2-0 up inside 20 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinicius Junior reduced the deficit in the 33rd minute and scored again to drag them level on 75 minutes, before Sakamoto’s controversial late winner.

Continue reading...
title: Raphinha sees red as Brazil stunned by Japan while Argentina’s post-Messi era starts with defeat

author: Simon Burnton
description:
• Updates from 1.30pm (GMT) kick-off at Stamford Bridge

  • Get in touch: email Simon and follow us on BlueSky

Manchester United are dominating so far, and Maya Le Tissier has now put them 1-0 up with an excellent shot from 20 yards or so that dips into the corner of the net.

Essential pre-match reading: here’s Suzanne Wrack’s preview of Chelsea v Manchester City:

There was a time when the games between the top three – traditionally Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal – were title-deciders. Where every point taken off a title rival was key. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League, it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique.

But when Chelsea welcome the title holders and current leagu
title: Chelsea v Manchester City: Women’s Super League – live

author: Greg Wood
description:
• First race gets under way at 12.35pm (all times GMT)

  • Paddy Power Gold Cup Steeplechase at 2.40pm

  • Share your thoughts with Greg via email

Just under 10 minutes to the off in the Triumph Hurdle Trial and there is still plenty of money for Atomic City, currently trading at around 11-8. Charles Darnay is attracting backers too, though, at 9-4, while Admiral Will Brown, who was rated 78 on the Flat and won his hurdles debut at Down Royal in October, is also lively in the market at 9-2.

There was fine display of jumping for the big Saturday crowd to enjoy in the opener, as Oran McGill got into an excellent rhythm on Dinoland and comfortably held Little Ledgend by six lengths.
title: Cheltenham November meeting horse racing – live

author: Sanya Mansoor in New York
description:
Members of Congress and advocates warn that returning people to their home countries could be a death sentence

Dozens of Afghans who are currently in the US but fear being deported back to Afghanistan along with a larger group and possibly killed by the Taliban are experiencing “fragile relief” this weekend after it appeared that the Trump administration had put on hold plans to remove them within days.

Members of Congress and advocates have repeatedly warned that the deportations could effectively be a death sentence.

Continue reading...
title: Trump ‘whiplash’ on deportations putting Afghans in turmoil: ‘People already survived a war’

author: Arwa Mahdawi
description:
House members have responded to legitimate criticism with cynicism. Let’s not have another ‘Bernie bros’ moment

Before we get started, some ground rules. You are, of course, completely free to disagree with everything I have to say here. However, doing so might mean that you’re racist, homophobic and/or sexist. (Not to boast, but I have a lot of oppression cards to play.) So, you might want to tread carefully, OK?

That might sound ridiculous, but I don’t make the rules: I’m just taking a page from the corporate Democrat playbook. From Haley Stevens to Hakeem Jeffries, cynically weaponizing identity politics to ward off reasonable criticism seems to be all the rage.

Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist

Continue reading...
title: Corporate Democrats are weaponizing identity politics to smear progressives | Arwa Mahdawi

author: Joe Pinner
description:
From a bamboo gym in Bali to a house made from earth in Wiltshire, these projects show the beauty in sustainable design

With construction accounting for more than a third of global emissions, sustainable architecture is central to the world meeting its climate targets. The following five creations from around the world exemplify how “green” buildings can also be beautiful.

Children’s Village, Tocantins, Brazil

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s an architect’s dream’: five beautiful eco buildings around the world

author: Jonathan Watts; graphics by Sara Fiorillo
description:
People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe

After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.

As Cop31 continues and scientists warn that climate breakdown may be accelerating, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.

Continue reading...
title: Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather

author: Luke Harding in Kyiv
description:
Throttling of Elon Musk’s military-grade satellite system affecting whole frontline, says Ukraine’s president

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused SpaceX of not telling the truth over restrictions to Ukraine’s Starshield satellite system, saying that the decision to impose speed limits appears to be “political” rather than “technical”.

Speaking on Friday, Ukraine’s president said the restrictions affecting Ukrainian drones had been in place for five days. They could no longer fly at speeds of more than 161km/h (100mph), he said, with connections at higher speeds lost.

Continue reading...
title: SpaceX not being honest about ‘political’ reasons for slowing Starshield, says Zelenskyy

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Activists dumped rocks off Norfolk coast on site of Burnham-backed project in protest against seabed trawling

The giant offshore windfarms backed by Andy Burnham this week may face unexpected stumbling blocks after Greenpeace activists unwittingly dumped about 15 tonnes of boulders on to the site as part of a campaign against seabed trawling in the North Sea.

Greenpeace created the “boulder barrier” to safeguard harbour porpoises off the Norfolk coast by dropping giant stone blocks, each weighing up to 2 tonnes, on to the sea floor to prevent a method of fishing known as bottom trawling.
title: Greenpeace boulders may delay building of £12bn windfarms in North Sea

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
The reprimand the defense secretary endured at US military’s most sacred shrine epitomizes his disrepute

The sentinel who bawled out Pete Hegseth for apparent disrespect at the Tomb of the Unknown Solider seemed to be speaking for more than just himself.

Nothing quite epitomizes the disrepute into which the US defense secretary has fallen than the reprimand delivered to Hegseth and his party after they conversed and laughed loudly while visiting Arlington national cemetery on Wednesday to mark Veterans’ Day.

Continue reading...
title: Hegseth survived impeachment bid but reprieve may be temporary: ‘He can’t escape justice forever’

author: Grace Holliday
description:
An ​e​lementary school ​w​atch party turned into a great opportunity to take a child’s-eye view of a spectacular astral phenomenon

Maurice Bakley was chaperoning an eclipse watch party at his son’s elementary school in Arlington, Virginia, when he took this photograph. As he had arrived early to fit his iPhone to a tripod to capture a time-lapse of the event (with the help of a monocular and a solar filter), he reached for his iPad for this shot.

“The boys in the photo, one of whom is my son, are part of a tight group of friends. They’ve known each other since kindergarten through their bilingual Spanish immersion school,” Bakley says. “They were eight and nine years old at the time, and none of them had ever seen an eclipse in real life.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘None of them had ever seen an eclipse in real life’: Maurice Bakley’s best phone picture

author: Donna Ferguson
description:
Comedian regrets ‘inappropriate’ jokes he made with Brand during work pair did together in the 2000s

The Great British Bake Off presenter Noel Fielding has said he was “horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand’s crimes” and has had no contact with his fellow comedian “for many years”.

In the early 2000s, Fielding often worked with Brand, who was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison on Monday for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

Continue reading...
title: Noel Fielding ‘horrified and deeply disturbed’ by Russell Brand’s crimes

author: Sophie McBain
description:
With authors losing lucrative deals and writers removed from prize shortlists, accusations of AI use are sending shock waves through the publishing industry. Is it too late to turn the tide on machine writing?

The romance novelist Coral Hart got her break writing books for Mills & Boon, the publisher of bodice-ripper paperbacks. In 2012, she decided to dip her toe in self-publishing. She felt drawn to dark romance, a subgenre featuring twisted, toxic love stories that was taking off online but that publishers didn’t want to touch. Three years later, things were going well enough that she decided to self-publish full-time.

Kindle Unlimited, where Hart sells her books, rewards prolific writers: the algorithm favours those who can produce a new book at least once a month. Hart says she knows of authors who hire more than a dozen ghostwriters to keep pace. By herself, Hart can write 10,000 words a day, but AI could help her produce many more. Since 2025
title: ‘It’s like the wild west’: how AI has rocked the literary world

author: Emillia Hawkins
description:
• All the latest news from around the footballing world

  • Get in touch: contact our matchday live writers on email

Before we go any further, here is a recap of what happened in the Nations League yesterday…

Well, it’s been quite the week, hasn’t it?

title: Pochettino to Manchester United latest, WSL and Nations League buildup – matchday live

author: Sid Lowe in Madrid
description:
Head coach hits out at ‘lies’ as suggestions of preferential treatment for young star overshadow preparations for England game in Madrid

From the London Palladium to Madrid’s Metropolitano, they’re all here. On Sunday night, the footballers who lifted the game’s biggest awards meet again three weeks later and on the field this time, dinner jackets but not a single man left behind. Harry Kane, the Ballon d’Or and Gerd Müller trophy winner. Unai Simón, holder of the Lev Yashin award. Luis de la Fuente, the coach of the year who on Thursday night announced that also joining them will be
title: De la Fuente feels the strain as Lamine Yamal club v country debate rages in Spain

author: Exclusive by Matt Hughes
description:
• ECB commits in principle to match in Victoria Falls

  • Drawn Test 30 years ago left David Lloyd fuming

England are set to play their first Test match in Zimbabwe since the infamous David Lloyd “we flippin’ murdered ’em!” series in 1996 in the next edition of the International Cricket Council’s future tours programme, covering 2027 to 2031.

During discussions with Zimbabwe Cricket at the ICC’s quarterly meeting in Bali this week, the England and Wales Cricket Board has committed in principle to visiting for a Test match during the next cycle, although a firm date has yet to be agreed.

Continue reading...
title: England ready to play first Test in Zimbabwe since bad-tempered 1996 tour

author: Charlotte Higgins
description:
Artists’ acts of remembrance about destruction and violence defy the dominant narratives of heroism and sacrifice

The way stories are told about wars really matters. It is a point powerfully made by the classical scholar Alice König who, in her work on ancient and modern warfare, points out that the way war is depicted and narrativised feeds into the way wars are actually conducted. Creating and absorbing a story (whether that is told in prose or poetry, or offered by an artwork or memorial) is more than packaging or reflecting on the past; it is about generating images and expectations, and about envisioning the future. Stories, she argues, influence real-world behaviours.

The war correspondent Christina Lamb has also
title: Power creates wars; wars create power. But these compelling acts of storytelling are breaking the loop | Charlotte Higgins

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Russia and US approach potential summit seeking China’s help to extricate them from wars of choice, as Putin hopes to find consensus on new global order

The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, is among those who have expressed concern that the world will witness a Yalta 2.0 moment if Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet trilaterally, as expected, on the sidelines of the Apec summit in China next week.

It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse.

Continue reading...
title: Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up?

author: Gwilym Mumford
description:
In this week’s newsletter: The deluge of whizzy production logos shown before films is a necessary annoyance – but there’s no excuse for them looking so naff

The outstanding release at the cinemas this week is Fjord, Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or winner about the travails of a conservative Romanian Christian family in a liberal Norwegian community. Starring Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve, it’s the sort of chewy, divisive drama that seems precision-tooled to stir spirited post-cinema debates. I’d heartily recommend seeing it, but with one small warning: you’ll to have to sit through a possibly unprecedented number of production logos and idents – those whizzy graphics advertising the help of a studio, film board, or mysterious financier – before the film finally starts.

You know the ones: a CGI leaf slowly floats towards the ground over gently plink-plonking piano, and
title: The Guide #269: The ident epidemic, and the true cost of movie-making

author: Lois Pryce
description:
A historic single-track train line through the foothills of the Pyrenees opens up a pristine wilderness of forests, gorges and thundering rivers

Alighting at the train station of Santa Linya in northern Spain, I paused to wonder what the railway engineers were thinking. A rough halt hewn out of the mountainside, with no ticket office, no waiting room, no sign of human habitation – just a single platform in the wilderness. On the far side of the track, a shimmering turquoise lake flanked by pine forests. Ahead – the only way out – a rocky trail snaking up the limestone cliff.

My husband and I had first strayed into this western corner of Catalonia – Pallars Jussà – on our honeymoon road trip 21 years earlier. Seduced by its dramatic landscape of canyons, lakes, crumbling ruins and the formidable Noguera Pallaresa river thundering south from the Pyrenees, we had vowed to return one day. He loves mountains, I love water, we both love abandoned buildings; it was a geographi
title: ‘Seduced by a dramatic landscape of canyons and lakes’: exploring Catalonia’s wild side

author: Thomas Eaton
description:
From four-year-old Binkie Stuart to Peter the cat, test your knowledge with the Saturday quiz

author: Rhik Samadder
description:
The amazing Ann Skelly plays Eve’s spy-handler Carolyn in a steamy, camp cold war thriller set in east Germany. Tagline: ‘everyone is watching – look hot!’

I always found it odd that spy stories are the quintessential interest of middle-aged men. Isn’t spying all about relationships, listening and choosing outfits? Is there something you’d like to tell us, men? Ironically, we don’t seem to have many ways of making you talk.

A female-forward spy story was the highlight of my week. Honey (Saturday 14 November, 9pm, BBC One) is a prequel to Killing Eve, and an origin story for one of its most intriguing characters: Fiona Shaw’s spy-handler Carolyn Martens. A title page lets us know that this is a period piece, while establishing a very un-period tone. We are in East Berlin, 1982, where the East German government run an ar
title: Honey: this flirty, kinky Killing Eve prequel should have been called Carré on Spying

title: One woman’s trash … the Edith Pritchett cartoon

author: Martin Pegan
description:
• Former batter said Hazlewood, Lyon and Starc not interviewed in 2018

  • Ex vice-captain claimed Cricket Australia ran ‘shoddy investigation’

David Warner has further fanned the flames on Australian cricket’s civil war as he claimed three of the bowlers who played in the third Test against South Africa in 2018 were not interviewed as part of a “shoddy” investigation into the sandpaper scandal.

The former Australia vice-captain said the ball tampering investigation “stinks of a cover up”, as he claimed on social media that the trio weren’t interviewed by Cricket Australia in the wake of Cameron Bancroft being spotted handling sandpaper on the field in Cape Town. The three players were part of a bowling quartet with Pat Cummins at the time.
title: ‘Stinks of a cover up’: David Warner fans flames with new sandpapergate claim

description:
Sean Duffy, Trump’s transportation secretary, acknowledges tech failure led federal aviation officials to shut down system and ground flights, though details are scarce

  • US aviation agency lifts nationwide ground stop affecting all air travel

  • Chaos at US airports as flight stoppage grinds travel plans to a halt

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

American Airlines says it will operate as many flights as possible on Friday night and try to recover st
title: US flight outage live updates: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop as airport chaos continues in US and beyond

author: Sean Ingle
description:
• Condition is prevalent in rugby and American football

  • Scientists are optimistic of significant breakthrough

Scientists have moved a step closer to diagnosing the degenerative brain condition chronic traumatic encephalopathy in living people, after a study found a blood biomarker that identifies an advanced form of the disease.

As things stand CTE, which is caused by repeated trauma to the head and is especially prevalent in collision and contact sports such as American football, rugby and football, can be diagnosed only after death by examining brain tissue.

Continue reading...
title: Scientists find blood biomarker that opens door to CTE diagnosis in living patients
